x: Commentary on Surah al-Buruj. In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Especially Merciful.
The discussion of the interpretation of the words of God, exalted is His majesty and sanctified are His names:

By the heaven containing constellations (1), and by the promised Day (2), and by a witness and that which is witnessed (3), may the people of the trench be destroyed (4), [the people of] the fire supplied with fuel (5).
Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him, said:
: Our Lord, majestic is His praise, swore by the heaven containing constellations.
The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of 'constellations' in this passage.
Some said that what is meant is: 'By the heaven containing palaces'; they said that al-buruj means palaces.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me: My father told me; my uncle told me; my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas,
m: . Ibn Abbas said: 'Palaces in the heaven.'
Another said: Rather, they are the stars.

c: I was informed from al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words,
: They claim that these are palaces in the heaven; it is also said that they are the stars.'

Mention of those who said this:

m: Muhammad ibn Amr related to me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us.

. He said: 'The constellations are the stars.'

Bishr related to us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah,
m: . He said: 'Its constellations are its stars.'
Others said that its meaning is instead: 'By the heaven containing sand and water.'

c: al-Hasan ibn Qara'ah related to me: Husayn ibn Numayr told us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn,
m: . He said: 'Containing sand and water.' The soundest of these opinions is that its meaning is: 'By the heaven containing the stations of the sun and the moon.' This is because al-buruj is the plural of burj, and these are elevated, lofty stations raised above the earth. This is also the sense of God's words,
Even if you were in lofty towers

[Qur'an 4:78].; and they are high, lofty stations in the heaven. There are twelve constellations: the moon travels through each one in two and one-third days, making twenty-eight stations; then it disappears
for two nights. The sun travels through each constellation in one month.

The correct position concerning this, in our view, is that one should say: God swore by a witness who bears witness and by something witnessed. He did not tell us, when swearing by them, which witness or which witnessed thing He intended. All the things we have mentioned as the scholars' interpretations are among those that may properly be called a witness and something witnessed.

x: May the people of the trench be destroyed
: He says: May the people of the trench be cursed.
said that the meaning of His words,
May the people of the trench be destroyed
, is a statement from God that the fire killed them.
The scholars differed over who the people of the trench were.
Some said: They were a people who belonged to the People of the Book, remnants of the Magians.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Humayd related to us: Ya'qub al-Qummi told us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza, who said:
m: When the Emigrants returned from one of their campaigns, news reached them of the death of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him.

x: Some of them said to one another: 'What rulings apply to the Magians, when they are not People of the Book, nor Arab polytheists?' Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: 'They were once People of the Book. Wine had been permitted to them, and one of their kings drank it until he became intoxicated. He then approached his sister and had intercourse with her. When the drunkenness had left him, he said to her: Woe to you! What way out is there for me from the predicament I have brought upon myself? She said: Address the people and say: O people, God has made marriage to sisters lawful. He stood up to address them and said: O people, God has made marriage to sisters lawful. The people said: We disavow this statement before God. No prophet brought it to us, and we have not found it in God's Book. He returned to her regretfully and said: Woe to you! The people refuse to accept this from me.

She said: Use the whips against them. He did so and used the whips against them, but they refused to accept it from him. He returned to her regretfully and said: They still refuse to accept it. She said: Address them again, and if they refuse, draw the sword against them. He did so, but the people still refused. He told her: The people have rejected it. She said: Dig a trench for them, then bring the inhabitants of your kingdom before it. Whoever accepts it, leave him; whoever does not, throw him into the fire. He did so. He brought the inhabitants of his kingdom before it, and whoever among them did not accept it, he threw into the fire. Then God revealed concerning them:
May the people of the trench be destroyed, the fire supplied with fuel
unless they believe in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy
Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women
then did not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of burning
From that time onward, they continued to regard marriage to sisters, daughters, and mothers as lawful.'

c: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah,
m: May the people of the trench be destroyed
. He said: 'It was related to us that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, used to say: They were people in the borderlands

of Yemen. The believers and unbelievers among them fought, and the believers prevailed over the unbelievers. Then they fought a second time, and the believers again prevailed over the unbelievers. Then they made pledges and covenants with one another that neither side would betray the other. But the unbelievers betrayed them and seized them violently. Then a man from among the believers said to them: Would you like a way to settle this? Light a fire, then bring us before it. Whoever follows your religion will be what you desire; whoever does not, let him leap into the fire, and you will be rid of him. They stoked a fire, and the believers were brought before it. Their leaders began leaping into it, until
there remained an old woman who seemed to hesitate
. A child in her lap said to her: Mother
, go forward and do not be a hypocrite.' God has related their story and their account to you.
Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us:

m: May the people of the trench be destroyed
. He said: 'He means the killers who killed them on the day they were killed.'
Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me:

m: May the people of the trench be destroyed, the fire supplied with fuel (4)

. He said: 'They were people from the Children of Israel. They dug a trench in the ground, then lit a fire in it. They stationed men and women beside that trench and brought them before the fire. They claimed that these were Daniel and his companions.'
Muhammad ibn Amr related to me:
Abu Asim told us: Isa told us.

m: All of them reported from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words,
May the people of the trench be destroyed
. He said: "There were fissures in the ground at Najran in which they used to torture people."
I was informed from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say:
"Ubayd told us: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words,
May the people of the trench be destroyed

: They claim that the people of the trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, then lit fires in it and made the believers stand beside it. They said: 'Either you renounce your faith, or we will throw you into the fire.'"
Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar related to me: Harami

c: Hammad ibn Salamah told us: Thabit al-Bunani told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Among the people who came before you there was a king who had a sorcerer. The sorcerer came to the king and said: 'I have grown old, and my appointed time is near. Give me a boy whom I can teach sorcery.'" He said: "So he gave him a boy to teach sorcery." He said: "The boy used to go regularly to the sorcerer, and between the sorcerer and the king there was a monk. Whenever the boy passed by the monk, he would sit with him and listen to his words, and he was impressed by what he heard. When the boy went to the sorcerer, the sorcerer would beat him and say: 'What kept you?' When he went home, he would sit with the monk and listen to his words; when he returned to his family, they would beat him and say: 'What kept you?' He complained about this to the monk, and the monk said to him: 'When the sorcerer asks you, 'What kept you?' say: 'My family kept me.' And when your family asks you: 'What kept you?' say: 'The sorcerer kept me.' While things were as they were, he was traveling along a road when he came upon a huge beast blocking the way and preventing the people from passing. The boy said: 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer's way or the monk's way is more pleasing to God.' He picked up a stone and said: 'O God, if the monk's way is more beloved to You than the sorcerer's way, then let me throw this stone and kill the beast so that the people may pass.' He threw it, killed the beast, and the people passed. The monk heard about this. The boy came to him, and the monk said: 'Boy, you are better than I am. You will be tested, so do not identify me.'" He said: "The boy used to cure those born blind, lepers, and people afflicted with other illnesses. The king had a courtier who became blind." He said: "Someone told him: 'There is a boy here who cures those born blind, lepers, and people with other illnesses. Why do you not go to him?'" He said: "So he prepared gifts for him." He said: "Then he went to the boy and said: 'Boy, if you cure me, all these gifts will be yours.' The boy replied: 'I do not cure you; rather, God is the One who cures. If you believe, I will call upon God to cure you.'" He said: "The blind man believed, and he called upon God, and God cured him. The blind man then sat with the king as he used to sit. The king said to him: 'Were you not blind?' He replied: 'Yes.' He said: 'Who cured you?' He replied: 'My Lord.' The king said: 'Do you have a lord besides me?' He replied: 'Yes. My Lord and your Lord is God.'" He said: "The king seized him and tortured him, saying: 'You must tell me who taught you this.' He identified the boy. The boy was summoned, and the king said: 'Return from your religion.' The boy refused. The king tortured him. The boy identified the monk. The monk was seized, and the king said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. The king placed a saw on the crown of his head and split him until it reached the ground. The king then seized the blind man and said: 'You must return, or I will kill you.' The blind man refused

. The king placed a saw on the crown of his head and split him until it reached the ground. Then he said to the boy: 'You must return, or I will kill you.' The boy refused. He said: "Take him to the top of the mountain
; if he renounces his religion, leave him, but if he does not, hurl him down."

When they reached the mountain peak with him, they all fell and died. The boy came walking until he entered the king's presence. The king said: 'Where are your companions?' He replied: 'God has spared me from them.' The king said: "Take him away, put him aboard a large ship

, and sail with him into the middle of the sea. If he renounces his religion, leave him; otherwise drown him." He said: "They took him away. When they reached the middle of the sea, the boy said: 'O God, spare me from them.' The ship overturned, and they all drowned. The boy came walking until he entered the king's presence. The king said: 'Where are your companions?' He replied: 'I called upon God, and He spared me from them.' The king said: 'I will kill you.' The boy replied: 'You cannot kill me until you do what I tell you.'" He said: "The boy told the king: 'Gather the people together in one open place, then crucify me. Take an arrow from my quiver, place it in the bow, and say: "In the name of the Lord of the boy." Then you will kill me.'" He said: "The king gathered the people together in one open place, crucified him, took an arrow from his quiver, placed it in the middle of the bow, then shot it, saying: 'In the name of the Lord of the boy.' The arrow struck the boy in his temple. The boy placed his hand on his temple in this way and died. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy.' They said to the king: 'What have you done? The very thing you feared has happened: the people have believed.' The king ordered the entrances to the roads to be seized

, then dug a trench and kindled fires in it. He seized the people and said: 'Whoever does not return [to the former religion], throw him into the fire.'" He said: "They began throwing them into the fire. A woman came with her infant child. When she was about to leap into it, she felt the heat of the fire and recoiled. Her child said to her: 'Mother
, go forward, for you are in the right.' So she leapt into the fire."
Others said: Rather, those whom the fire burned were the unbelievers who persecuted the believers.

x: Mention of those who said this:

c: I was informed from Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said:
m: "The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from the people during the interval between prophets

. A tyrant who worshipped idols sent for them and invited them to enter his religion, but they refused. He dug a trench and kindled a fire in it, then gave them the choice between entering his religion and being thrown into the fire. They chose to be thrown into the fire rather than abandon their religion. They were thrown into it, but God saved the believers who had been thrown into the fire from being burned: He took their souls before the fire could touch them. The fire then spread to the unbelievers standing at the edge of the trench and burned them. This is the meaning of God's words:
For them is the punishment of Hell
and for them is the punishment of burning
The scholars differed concerning the location of the answer to the oath in His words,

x: Some said that its answer is:
Indeed, the grip of your Lord is severe
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr related to us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, who said:
m: Indeed, the grip of your Lord is severe
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The oath is, God knows best, answered by
May the people of the trench be destroyed
. The emphatic lām is implicit, just as in
By the sun and its morning brightness
Successful indeed is the one who purifies it

[Qur'an 91:9]. The intended meaning, God willing, is: 'Indeed, successful is the one who purifies it,' with the lām omitted. If you wish, you may also say that the wording is arranged by anticipation, as though it said: 'The people of the trench were destroyed, by the heaven containing constellations.'

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa
said: In interpretation, the answer to the oath is found in His words,
May the people of the trench be destroyed
By the sun and its morning brightness
. This is the interpretation. He said

: We have not found the Arabs leaving an oath without a lām introducing its answer, or without 'no', 'indeed', or 'what'. If this is so, it is as though the answer has been omitted and the position of the answer then resumed with a declarative statement, as happens in many expressions such as 'O human being'. In my view, the most correct of these opinions is that of the one who said that the answer to the oath has been left unstated and that the following statement begins a new report. This is because the Arabs do not omit the marker of an oath's answer from speech when they do answer it.
Of the two interpretations of His words,
May the people of the trench be destroyed

, the more correct is: May the people of the trench who threw believing men and women into the trench be cursed. I have said that this is the sounder of the two interpretations because of the reason we cited from al-Rabi': God informed us that they have the punishment of burning in addition to the punishment of Hell. If they had not been burned in this world, His words
and for them is the punishment of burning

would have no intelligible meaning alongside His statement that they have the punishment of Hell, since the punishment of Hell is itself a punishment by fire, along with its other forms of punishment in the Hereafter. The trench (al-ukhdud) is a pit dug into the ground.

He says: It has indeed reached you, and you know it. So be patient in the face of your people's harm toward you and the distress they have caused you, just as the messengers against whom these hosts united were patient. Do not let their actions turn you away from conveying My message to them, just as those messengers were not turned away when they were sent to these people. The end for those among them who do not believe you and do not affirm you will be ruin and destruction, like what happened to these hosts. Rather, those who disbelieve are in denial (19), while God encompasses them from behind (20). Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an (21), in a Preserved Tablet (22).

God, exalted is His mention, says: The reason these people deny God's warning is not that accounts of the nations who came before them and denied God's messengers—such as Pharaoh and his people, Thamud, and those like them—and of the punishments God inflicted upon them for denying the messengers have failed to reach them.
Rather, they are in denial of God's revelation and His sending it down, preferring their own desires and following the ways of their forefathers.
And God encompasses them from behind
: He encompasses their deeds and has counted them; none of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for all of them.
Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an
: He, majestic is His praise, thereby refutes those who call the Qur'an poetry and rhymed prose. It is not as they claim; rather, it is a noble Qur'an.

, meaning that the Tablet is what is described as preserved. If so, the interpretation is: in a Tablet preserved from additions to it or subtractions from it, beyond what God recorded in it.
Ibn Muhaysin among the Meccan reciters and Nafi' among the Medinan reciters read it in the nominative,
